svg.title: Why a backdoor link beats the VPN path, and how a sham link restores a fair comparison
svg.desc: Left panel shows the preference order used by OSPF: intra-area first, then inter-area, then external routes, with cost only compared inside the same class. A backdoor link between two sites makes the remote prefix look intra-area, so it wins even when the VPN path is faster. Right panel shows the sham link: a loopback-to-loopback tunnel across the MPLS VPN that is advertised into OSPF as an intra-area link, so the VPN path is now also intra-area and the comparison falls back to cost. Three prerequisites are listed for the sham link to come up: the same area, matching authentication, and the endpoints reachable through the VPN rather than the core. A closing note explains the design decision: use the sham link when the customer insists on OSPF at the PE-CE and a backdoor exists, otherwise choose eBGP and delete the problem.
svg.text: OSPF compares route class before it compares cost — that is the whole problem
A sham link does not change the metric; it changes which class the VPN path belongs to
THE PREFERENCE ORDER
1. Intra-area (O)
2. Inter-area (O IA)
3. External (E1 / E2)
Class wins first. Cost only breaks ties inside a class.
Without the sham link
Site A learns site B's prefix two ways:
· via the VPN: OSPF inter-area from PE2
· via the backdoor: OSPF intra-area, cost 50
The backdoor wins even if its cost is worse, and it
carries traffic the VPN was built to carry.
With the sham link
A tunnel between PE1 and PE2 loopbacks, carried
inside the VPN, advertised into OSPF as a normal
link — so the VPN path becomes intra-area too.
Now both paths are in the same class, so plain cost
decides. The design regains control of the comparison.
THREE PREREQUISITES, ALL MANDATORY
1. Both ends in the same OSPF area — a mismatch leaves the adjacency down and looks like a routing fault.
2. Matching authentication on both ends, including key ID and key chain, or the tunnel never comes up.
AND THE THIRD, WHICH IS A DESIGN QUESTION RATHER THAN A CONFIG LINE
3. The tunnel endpoints must be reachable through the VPN, not through the core IGP — otherwise the sham link rides on the very path it is meant to override.
